newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian base metals steady, industrial demand low.
newsitem.headline: Indian base metals steady, industrial demand low.

text.p: Indian base metals on Wednesday remained steady in a narrow trading range with demand from industrial consumers low but limited arrivals and a shortage of nearby supplies keeping prices at last levels, dealers said.
Copper was steady at 13,500 rupees, zinc at 7,750 rupees and lead at 4,550 rupees per quintal.
"The end of the financial year is around the corner and major players kept to the sidelines as they were busy with their books of account," said Sharad Parikh, president of Bombay Metal Exchange.
"The turnover remained slow and will remain slow upto month end but on April 1 am expecting more activity and firm price trend," he added.

Nickel was steady at the reduced level of 37,100 rupees per quintal after losing 200 rupees on Tuesday. Aluminium was quiet at 7,425 rupees and tin consolidated gains at 31,600 rupees per quintal on limited supplies. Tin was up by 400 rupees per quintal last week.
